prompt: Compose an entirely ORIGINAL 80-second instrumental soundtrack for ThaiNative, an adorable chibi Thai-folklore turn-based artillery RPG. Charming magical moonlit adventure, playful courage, light rhythmic energy about 96 BPM, never threatening or aggressive. The clearly identifiable lead instruments must be Thai ranat ek wooden xylophone, chakhe plucked zither, khlui phiang aw bamboo flute, saw duang bowed fiddle; supporting sparse khong wong gong accents, soft taphon hand drum and delicate ching. Natural acoustic timbres, no Western orchestral strings/brass, no electronic dance beats, no piano or music box, no vocals or chanting. Four varied connected sections: 0-20s bouncy ranat introduces a graceful long melody with chakhe answer; 20-40s flute leads a completely new soaring melody over soft syncopated taphon; 40-60s a quieter contrasting saw-duang lyrical phrase with spacious chakhe and gong; 60-80s return with a fresh interwoven flute/ranat variation and gentle cadence that flows back to the opening. Change orchestration or melodic contour every 8 bars; never loop a short motif endlessly. Sound like tiny spirit friends playfully sparring under golden lanterns, warm and enchanting. Moderate dynamics so impacts and game UI remain clear. No sudden loud climax, no sound effects, no quotation of existing music.
